In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the development of tuning rules for PI control that are applicable to a wider class of processes than the original Ziegler‐ Nichols rules.
the question of how to tune a PI controller to achieve a specified performance for a process that has a time delay and a first‐order lag.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ziegler-Nichols frequency response method is a useful tuning method only for processes that are not lag dominated.
the Ziegler–Nichols tuning rules are not applicable for processes that are lag‐dominated or have a short time delay.
the Ziegler–Nichols frequency response tuning method is not a good tuning method, but that it can be improved by a simple modification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ziegler-Nichols tuning rules for PI controllers should not be used for tuning of processes with time delays.
the Ziegler-Nichols frequency response method is not a good method for tuning PI control.
the Ziegler–Nichols rules should only be used for the tuning of PI controllers if the time delay is short.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to know the limitations of the tuning rules before using them.
the Ziegler–Nichols rules are not as general as is often claimed.
a frequency response analysis of the closed‐loop system should always be used for tuning PI controllers.
